title: Keep fact, interpretation and opinion apart
statement: Keep fact, interpretation, opinion and uncertainty distinct in what learners read and in the conclusions they frame, so they can tell what kind of claim each statement is.
detail: The course-plan quality standard lists preserving the distinctions among fact, interpretation, opinion and uncertainty among its obligations for domain-bearing content (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, Q047). It accepts such content only when fact-versus-interpretation labels and epistemic review cover every governed claim, chart, item and feedback line, and counts a contested view presented as fact among its failure signals. Present a contested matter as open, never as settled, and keep a made-up teaching case apart from real evidence. In history, bound each claim by who, where, when and which source.
against: none found; the standard applies it only where externally checkable domain claims appear (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`).

A passage should not present a matter as settled where that is unwarranted. Distinguishing fact, interpretation, and opinion is part of the discipline itself.
The scientific process distinguishes observation, hypothesis, theory, consensus, measurement, and related categories; student writing should make clear which of these the student is doing.
no model presented as literal reality;
no contested interpretation presented as settled fact.
the coach coaches, the book reader reads, and keeping the two voices distinct is how a student hears 'the story' and 'the teaching' as separate things.
its first unit mixes a made-up teaching case with real evidence and the two must be audibly distinguishable.
